title: Hub client follows cross-origin redirects with no SSRF guard (malicious/compromised hub reaches the install's private network)
description: Every hub request goes through reach()/hubFetch() using the global fetch() with its default redirect:"follow". The hub base URL is validated once at join time (checkHubUrl), but after that the install trusts the hub completely and follows any 3xx Location it returns to ANY host. hubPicture() (kind "listing"/"photo"/"figure", lines 680-708) fetches images this way, stores the bytes locally, and serves them at /api/listing-photos, /api/hub-photos, /api/figures. A hub that answers /v1/listing-photos/:id (or any hubFetch route) with a 302 to an internal address (http://127.0.0.1:*, http://169.254.169.254/…, a Railway private service) makes the bench server issue that GET. safe-fetch.ts (used only by downloadManualLink) blocks private addresses and re-checks every redirect, but the hub image/JSON client has none of that protection. The Authorization: Bearer <installKey> header is dropped by undici on the cross-origin hop, so the key is not leaked, but the internal GET still happens and its response body is cached and rendered to signed-in users as an image (imageResponse forces image/* + nosniff + CSP sandbox, so it is not XSS, but the raw bytes are shown).
failure_scenario: An install admin joins (or is tricked via a stitchhub: invite into joining) a hub the attacker controls, or the legitimate hub is compromised. The hub returns 302 Location: http://127.0.0.1:5733/… (an internal service or cloud metadata endpoint) for a listing/figure/photo fetch. The bench server (on Railway or the shop LAN) issues the GET to that internal host and stores/serves the response. Reproduced locally: joined a private bench to a hub simulator; GET /api/listing-photos/evilphoto1 caused the bench to fetch http://127.0.0.1:5733/latest/meta-data/… and return the internal service's body 'INTERNAL-ONLY: db_password=hunter2' as image/jpeg.
suggested_fix: Give the hub client the same protection safe-fetch already implements: set redirect:"manual" (or "error") on the hub fetch and either refuse redirects outright or only follow them when the new URL's origin equals the configured hub origin; and/or route hub fetches through the safe-fetch private-address lookup. Do not blindly follow hub-supplied Location headers to arbitrary hosts.
evidence: reach() in src/lib/hub.ts:153-160 calls `fetch(url, { ...rest, signal: ... })` with no `redirect` option (defaults to follow) and no address check. Test output: bench log shows `hub: GET /v1/listing-photos/evilphoto1` then `INTERNAL service hit: GET /latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials auth: (none)`, and the Playwright request `GET /api/listing-photos/evilphoto1 200 image/jpeg "INTERNAL-ONLY: db_password=hunter2"`. Contrast src/lib/safe-fetch.ts:44-53,96-105 which resolves+blocks private IPs and re-checks each hop.
verifier_notes: confirmed: Accurate. reach() in src/lib/hub.ts:153 calls fetch() with the default redirect:'follow' and checks no addresses. checkHubUrl only validates the configured base once. /api/listing-photos/[id] lets any signed-in user trigger hubPicture('listing', id) for any id that passes hubId, and the bytes are stored in ListingPhoto and served back. safe-fetch's private-address and per-hop checks apply only to manual-link downloads, and neither prior round (8b3e5f2, 9ba25a4) touched hub redirects. undici drops the Authorization header on the cross-origin hop, so the install key does not leak. From the hub's side the request is blind: it cannot read the reply. But on a hosted install with ALLOW_SIGNUP a hub operator can sign up a shop and read the cached reply at /api/listing-photos/<id>, which makes it a full-read SSRF into the deployment's private network. A 307/308 on a hubFetch POST would also re-send the JSON body to the internal host. Precondition: a malicious or compromised hub. So medium.

title: Order for a listing that was already removed locally is saved with no company and nobody sees it (multi-company install)
description: saveOrder finds the owning company of a new sale only from the local Listing row (`owner = (await db.listing.findUnique({ where: { id: o.listingId } }))?.shopId`), then falls back to soleShopId(), which is null when an install has more than one company. removeListing deletes the local listing row straight away (market.ts:109), and a REMOVED listing arriving in the feed is deleted too (hub.ts:482-484). The hub does not refuse removal while orders are open. So if a buyer orders and the seller removes the listing before the next sync (every 10 minutes), the order is stored with shopId NULL. It is missing from /market/orders for every company, its page returns 404, and it can never be claimed, because `have?.shopId` stays null on later updates. The buyer waits on REQUESTED forever. The same attribution gap orphans a buyer's order when placeOrder's response is lost (the order still exists on the hub; placeOrder has no idempotency key, so a retry also makes a duplicate). It also orphans a listing when createListing's response is lost: it arrives through sync as mine with shopId null, no company can see or manage it, and it can still be ordered.
failure_scenario: On the shared multi-company install, my company listed an item. Another hub member ordered it through the API. I then removed the listing in the UI and pressed 'Check for updates' on /market/orders?role=seller. The sale does not appear, and /market/orders/<id> returns 404. The DB row has shopId NULL.
suggested_fix: Keep the owner on the hub: send a shopRef with createListing and placeOrder, and have the hub return it on listings and orders (see the identity finding). As a short-term fix, keep a tombstone for removed listings, e.g. mark the local row REMOVED instead of deleting it, so saveOrder can still find the company. Refuse DELETE /v1/listings/:id on the hub while REQUESTED/ACCEPTED/PAID orders exist (or have it decline them). Add a client idempotency key to POST /v1/orders and /v1/listings, as posts already have with clientId.
evidence: Reproduced (scratchpad orphan.js): output `order 200 5b9cf7027eb243ebaf6213cb SH-000006`, `seller sees order on /market/orders?role=seller: false`, `seller order page status: 404`. `select id,number,role,status,"shopId" from "MarketOrder" where id='5b9cf7027eb243ebaf6213cb'` => `5b9cf...|SH-000006|seller|REQUESTED|` (shopId empty). I then cancelled the order as the buyer to clean up.
verifier_notes: confirmed: saveOrder (hub.ts:529-535) takes the owner from have?.shopId, then the shopId argument (only placeOrder passes one), then the local Listing row's shopId, then soleShopId(). pullOrders calls saveOrder(o) with no shopId. removeListing deletes the local Listing row right after the hub DELETE (market.ts:109), and the hub's DELETE /v1/listings/:id does not check for open orders (market.mjs ownListing plus UPDATE status='REMOVED'). On an install with more than one company, soleShopId() returns null. The sale is then stored with shopId NULL and stays that way, because later updates recompute the same null. Every reader filters by shopId: orders list, order page, invoice, market-todo and ownOrder. No code ever assigns an orphaned MarketOrder. The buyer can still cancel from their side, so medium fits.
also_reported_as: qa: src/lib/hub.ts:532 Multi-company install: a sale on a listing that no longer exists locally gets no company and is invisible to everyone
qa: src/lib/hub.ts:532 On a multi-company install, a sale whose listing was removed before sync is saved with no company and nobody can see or answer it

title: Leaving and rejoining the hub, or moving to another hub, orphans the shop's own listings, orders and notes and keeps stale rows from the old hub
description: leaveHub clears the install key and cursors but keeps every synced Listing, MarketOrder, ManualLink and HubPost row. joinHub registers a brand-new install (new installId and key) and restarts the cursors at 0. After a rejoin, the next sync recomputes 'mine' against the new install, so the shop's own listings become another shop's: they disappear from My listings, can't be edited or removed (the hub answers 403), and the shop can order from itself. Open orders now belong to the old install, so every order action gets 404 and they are stranded. Rows the new hub doesn't have (after joining a different hub) are never removed: they show on /market and /links, and acting on them fails. The 'Leave the hub' confirm (src/app/(app)/settings/page.tsx:53) says only 'Disconnect from the hub?' and nothing blocks leaving with active listings or open orders. tests/hub.spec.ts leaves and rejoins on every run, so the shared e2e environment keeps accumulating this state.
failure_scenario: A shop with 4 active listings and an open sale clicks Leave the hub, then joins again with the same invite. My listings shows 0. Browse shows its own listing as another shop's with a Send order form, and the order goes through (the shop buys from itself). The open sale can no longer be accepted or shipped from the bench.
suggested_fix: On leave, or on joining a different hub URL, delete the synced copies (ManualLink, HubPost/HubPhoto, Listing, ListingPhoto, XPart, HubFigure) and mark local MarketOrders archived. Refuse to leave while the install has ACTIVE listings or open orders, or warn clearly in the confirm. Better still, keep and reuse the install key when rejoining the same hub instead of registering a new install.
evidence: rejoin.js on my instance: 'my listings after rejoin: 0', 'own old listing shown in Browse as another shop: 1', 'has Send order form: 1 | has edit form: 0', 'after ordering own listing: /market/orders/e3504c2b50bb4eca820201bd []'. DB: all 'QA price…' rows mine=f. After my hub's DB was wiped and I rejoined, /market still listed 'R bobbin case' and 'X cheap motor'; ordering one gave 'That listing isn't on the hub.' /links still showed 6 stale links.
verifier_notes: confirmed: Confirmed. leaveHub (src/lib/hub.ts:269-277) clears only the key and cursors. joinHub registers a brand-new install and resets the cursors, and keeps the synced Listing and MarketOrder rows. On re-sync, saveListing overwrites mine with the value computed against the new install id (false). My listings filters mine=true, so the company's own listing disappears. The listing page's sameInstall check needs found.mine, so the Send order form appears. The hub allows the order because install_id differs from the new install. Open orders belong to the old install, so the hub answers 404 to every step. The confirm says only 'Disconnect from the hub?'. This is a less common, admin-only flow, so medium fits.

title: A tech can set the shop's marketplace payment instructions (admin-only in Settings) by accepting an order
description: orderAction only calls requireUser(), so any role can accept marketplace sales. When the shop has no saved payInstructions, accepting an order also writes the typed text into Shop.payInstructions (line 199). In Settings that field is only editable through saveShop, which requires requireAdmin. A TECH can therefore choose where the shop's marketplace money goes: for that order (the invoice's 'How to pay') and, when the field was empty, for every later order, because the accept form pre-fills the shop value for the owner.
failure_scenario: Owner adds a TECH user. The tech opens Marketplace > Orders > Selling > order SH-000008, types 'PayPal: tech.personal@evil.test' in 'How they pay you' and clicks Accept. The buyer's invoice says to pay the tech's PayPal, and Shop.payInstructions is now that text for all future sales.
suggested_fix: Only update Shop.payInstructions when the user is admin/owner (requireAdmin). For techs, either use the saved shop value only (ignore typed text) or require admin to accept sales and create listings. At least log who changed pay instructions per order.
evidence:
pw1/pw2.cjs on :3100 as TECH qa-hcm1t-muiw6y8g@test.local: 'accepted by TECH'.
DB after: Shop 'E2E Test Shop' (cmuiw673b...) payInstructions = 'PayPal: tech.personal@evil.test (NOT the shop)'
Hub order SH-000008: pay_instructions = 'PayPal: tech.personal@evil.test (NOT the shop)'.
Code: `const pay = str(formData.get("payInstructions")) ?? shop.payInstructions; ... if (!shop.payInstructions) await db.shop.update({ ... data: { payInstructions: pay } });` while settings.ts saveShop uses requireAdmin().
verifier_notes: confirmed: orderAction (market.ts:189-199) only calls requireUser() and ownOrder(). On accept it uses the typed payInstructions ahead of the shop's saved value, and if Shop.payInstructions is empty it saves the typed text there. In Settings that field can only be changed through saveShop, which uses requireAdmin() (settings.ts:24,46). The accept form's textarea (orders/[id]/page.tsx:127) is shown to every role. So a TECH can always put their own payment text on an order they accept, and on a shop that has none saved yet they also set the admin-only shop-wide value that later accept forms pre-fill. This is an insider (same-shop employee) risk, so the impact is limited, but money goes wherever that text says.
also_reported_as: security: src/actions/market.ts:199 A TECH can silently set shop-wide payment instructions and redirect marketplace payments when accepting an order
code: src/actions/market.ts:199 A TECH can set the shop's marketplace payment instructions (an owner/admin-only setting) and send buyers' payments anywhere

title: Multi-company install: every company's listings, sales, purchases, notes and ratings go to the hub under the name of the company whose admin joined
description: The hub connection belongs to the whole install. The install is registered under the joining admin's shop name (src/actions/hub.ts:32 joinHub(..., shop.name, ...)). The hub then stamps that one name on everything the install sends: listings (stitchhub src/market.mjs:230 shop_name = inst.name), orders (market.mjs:321-334 seller_shop/buyer_shop = installs.name) and notes (server.mjs:406-408 shop_name = inst.name). createListing and placeOrder send no per-company identity. Reputation is per install, so star ratings for every company's sales and purchases are pooled into one score. The bench shows these hub names as the company's identity: the invoice header is o.sellerShop (src/app/(app)/market/orders/[id]/invoice/page.tsx:30), with company B's own address, email and phone from sellerContact underneath. Round 1 said every market listing and order is scoped to the signed-in company. That scoped what each company can see locally, but not the identity sent to the hub, so the fix is incomplete. Related symptom: HubPost.mine is install-level, so company B also gets a Remove button on company A's notes (src/components/shared-posts.tsx:77), which fails when clicked.
failure_scenario: On a hosted install with QA Shop A (joined the hub) and QA Shop B: B lists 'Company B walking foot'. Every other hub member sees it as sold by 'QA Shop A'. A remote shop orders it and B accepts. B's invoice is headed 'QA Shop A' with B's address and B's Zelle details. The buyer's order shows sellerShop 'QA Shop A'. Ratings of B's sale count toward A's reputation. B's shared notes appear as 'QA Shop A'.
suggested_fix: Carry the company's identity on each hub object. Send shopName (and a stable per-company seller key) with POST /v1/listings, /v1/orders and /v1/posts; have the hub store it and key reputations on (install, company). Alternatively register one hub install per company. As a stop-gap, head the invoice with sellerContact.name instead of sellerShop, and show Remove on a hub note only when the SharedPost with that hubId belongs to the viewer's shop (or the viewer is a platform admin).
evidence: Ran against my own app (port 6417, two companies on one install) and my own hub (port 6418). Hub feed: '8ccd43a5801348698a0b1ed5:QA Shop A:Company B walking foot'. Order: 'sellerShop as buyer sees it: QA Shop A'. B invoice header: "QA Shop A 99 B Street, Btown 555-0102 · b@shopb.test Invoice SH-000003". Buyer R sees: 'QA Shop A {"name":"QA Shop B","email":"b@shopb.test",...} pay: Company B Zelle 555-0102'. Company B on /shared sees 1 Remove button on A's note; clicking it gives 'Only whoever shared this note, or their shop's owner or admin, can remove it.'
verifier_notes:
confirmed: Confirmed. On a multi-company install only the StitchBench administrator can join the hub (requireInstallAdmin), and joinHub registers the install under that admin's shop name (src/actions/hub.ts:32). Hub POST /v1/listings (stitchhub market.mjs:230) stores inst.name as shop_name. POST /v1/orders (market.mjs:334) stores installs.name as seller_shop/buyer_shop. POST /v1/posts (server.mjs:406-408) stores inst.name. Ratings are keyed on rated_install_id. createListing, placeOrder and pushPending send no per-company identity. The invoice header is o.sellerShop (invoice/page.tsx:30). shared-posts.tsx:77 shows Remove whenever p.mine, which is install-level. Round 1 scoped only what each company sees locally. The shared env shows it too: the orphan listing 'QA orphan test MUIN82DG' made on the 3100 install sits on the hub as 'E2E Test Shop'. Severity recalibrated from high to medium: the data is misattributed (seller name on listings, orders, invoices and notes; pooled reputation), but no other company's private data leaks and no money total is wrong. Payment instructions and contact details stay the right company's.
confirmed: The claim describes the code correctly and I reproduced it on the shared install. The hub stamps the install's registration name on everything that install sends: listings (market.mjs:230), orders (market.mjs:321-334, seller.name / me.name from installs) and notes (server.mjs posts shop_name = inst.name). stitchbench sends no per-company identity. createListing only sends the listing fields; placeOrder puts the company only inside buyerContact.name. Reputations are keyed on rated_install_id (market.mjs:42-48), so all companies' ratings are pooled into one score. The invoice header is o.sellerShop (invoice/page.tsx:30), and the company's own sellerContact appears under it. The Remove symptom is also accurate. shared-posts.tsx:77 shows Remove whenever HubPost.mine is true, and that flag is install-wide. removeHubPost (hub.ts:143-156) then refuses anyone outside the note's own company unless they are a platform admin. Round 1 (8b3e5f2) only scoped local visibility and ownership, and the hub commit (28842a1) didn't touch identity. So this is still open.

I rated it medium rather than high. It needs a multi-company install that has joined the hub as a member, and it only affects companies other than the one that joined. INSTALL.md documents that setup, but it isn't the default single-shop one. No company can read or change another company's private rows. The harm is misattribution: every hub member sees the wrong seller or buyer name, the invoice shows the wrong business name, and one company's ratings raise or lower another's reputation. The impersonation angle is real but depends on who can create companies. Companies are added by a platform admin, or by anyone only when ALLOW_SIGNUP=true, which INSTALL.md says to leave unset. A company made that way can publish listings and notes under the host shop's name and reputation, and payment goes to its own payment details. One more consequence the reviewer didn't mention: because the self-order check is install-level (market.mjs 'You can't order your own listing'), two companies on the same install can't trade with each other on the marketplace.
also_reported_as: qa: src/actions/market.ts:67 Every company on a shared install sells, buys and is rated under one hub identity (install name and install reputation)

title: Editing a listing silently ignores a bad price or quantity, wipes the flat shipping rate on a typo, and allows a $0 price
description: updateListing sends a price only when toCents parses it, and a qty only when int(...) >= 0. Anything else is dropped silently and the toast still says 'Listing updated'. Shipping is sent whenever the field is present, so an unparseable value becomes shippingCents: null, which turns a flat rate into 'Quoted with the invoice'. Price 0 is accepted on edit, although createListing refuses 0. Negative values reach the hub and come back as 'The price is whole cents, 0 or more.', which uses the API's units rather than dollars.
failure_scenario: A seller changes a listing from $7.50 + $2.00 shipping, typing 'abc' as the price, '-1' as the quantity and 'abc' as the shipping. They see 'Listing updated'. Price and quantity are unchanged, but the flat $2.00 shipping has been removed from the stored listing. Typing 0 as the price makes the item free.
suggested_fix: Validate like createListing does. A non-empty field that doesn't parse, or a price <= 0, or a negative qty, raises a UserError in dollars ('Enter the price in dollars, e.g. 12.50'). Clear shipping only when the field is truly blank.
evidence: upd.js on my instance: input {price:'abc',qty:'-1',ship:'abc'} -> toasts ['Listing updated'], after: 'PRICE EACH $7.50 AVAILABLE 3 SHIPPING Quoted with the invoice'. {price:'0'} -> ['Listing updated'], after 'PRICE EACH $0.00'. {price:'-4'} -> ['The price is whole cents, 0 or more.'].
verifier_notes: confirmed: Confirmed. updateListing (src/actions/market.ts:86-103) drops an unparseable price or qty without error. It sends shippingCents = toCents(...) whenever the field is present, so a typo becomes null and clears the flat rate. It accepts price 0, which createListing refuses (<= 0). Negative values reach the hub's cents-worded message. The success toast shows regardless. This matches the rubric's 'missing validation that stores bad data'.

title: Offline mode is incomplete: sharing a note and 'Check for updates' still wait the full 30 s every time when the hub hangs
description: Round 2 promised that once the hub stops answering, anything a person asks of it says 'No connection to the community hub' within seconds. But syncHub() always runs inBackground (src/lib/hub.ts:673), which skips the 15 s offline short-circuit and the 4 s health check. sharePost saves the note locally and then awaits syncHub() (shared.ts:43). With a silent hub, /v1/me waits its full 30 s timeout every time, even when the install already knows the hub is down. The same applies to refreshOrders ('Check for updates', market.ts:247), Settings 'Sync now' (hub.ts:41), and the post-accept and post-cancel sync (market.ts:240), which also waits for any long sync already running. tests/offline.spec.ts covers only partner Sync now and createListing.
failure_scenario: The shop's internet line goes silent (packets dropped). A tech shares a note: the Share button shows 'Saving...' for 30 s. They share another one a minute later, when the install already shows 'Offline since', and it takes 30 s again. 'Check for updates' on Orders likewise takes 30 s before saying there is no connection.
suggested_fix: In sharePost (and after accept or cancel), don't await the sync. Fire it in the background with void syncHub().catch(...), or await it only when hubOfflineSince() is null. For user-pressed Sync and Check for updates, apply the same quick offline check as reach() before starting a full sync, and add these actions to tests/offline.spec.ts.
evidence: Hub frozen with SIGSTOP (the 'hang' case). share.js twice in a row: 'share answered in 30664 ms ["Shared with every shop"]' and 'share answered in 30668 ms'. hang2.js: 'check for updates 30670 ms ["No connection to the community hub right now ..."]'. Online baseline: 'share answered in 369 ms'.
verifier_notes: confirmed: Confirmed, and it makes the round-2 offline fix incomplete. syncHub() always runs inBackground (hub.ts:673), so reach() skips the 15 s offline short-circuit and the 4 s /health check. Every hubFetch in doSync then waits the full 30 s AbortSignal timeout on a silent hub. sharePost awaits syncHub() (shared.ts:43). refreshOrders (market.ts:247), syncCommunityHub and accept/cancel do the same. It happens again even when offlineSince is already set. A non-sync hub action answers at once in the same state, which isolates the cause. The share is still saved locally, so the harm is a 30 s wait on everyday buttons whenever the line is silent. Medium.
also_reported_as: code: src/actions/shared.ts:43 Share, accept/cancel and join run the whole hub sync while the person waits, bypassing the round-2 offline fast-fail

title: Any user (including techs, on any company of a shared install) can remove a community cross-reference entry, and StitchBench has no way to see or restore removed entries
description: removeCrossRef needs only requireUser(). It sends DELETE /v1/xparts/:id and deletes the local copy. Every other install deletes its copy on the next sync (saveXParts removes deleted parts). The hub keeps the row and has POST /v1/xparts/:id/restore, but the app never calls it. /xref/<id> of a removed entry is 404, so its History and 'Roll back' buttons can't be reached. The file header and README promise 'every change keeps the whole entry... any version can be restored', but in practice one click by any user removes a community part for all shops, recoverable only by someone with API access.
failure_scenario: A TECH user on a hosted install opens Cross-reference > entry > Remove > 'Remove for everyone?'. The part disappears from every shop, and /xref/<id> answers 404 on every install. The hub row is deleted=true with revisions 'added' then 'removed', and there is no UI to restore it.
suggested_fix: Keep removed entries locally (soft-deleted, hidden from search) and add a 'Recently removed' list on /xref with a Restore button (POST /v1/xparts/:id/restore). Consider requiring admin/owner for Remove and Merge, and showing who removed it.
evidence: pw3.cjs on :3100 as TECH: after remove, /xref/<id> status: 404. Hub: 0edd34086b574b678a304999|t; revisions: added|QA Tech|E2E Test Shop, removed|QA Tech|E2E Test Shop. grep: no caller of /restore for xparts in src/.
verifier_notes: confirmed: The finding describes the code correctly. removeCrossRef (src/actions/xref.ts:71-77) calls only requireUser(), so any role in any company on the install can use it. It sends DELETE /v1/xparts/:id and then deletes the local row. saveXParts (src/lib/hub.ts:457-459) deletes every entry the hub marks deleted, so each other install drops it within its 10-minute sync. /xref/[id]/page.tsx:21-22 calls notFound() when there is no local row, so the History panel and 'Roll back' can no longer be reached. Nothing in src/ calls POST /v1/xparts/:id/restore, and the hub admin UI (public/admin.html) and admin routes have no restore either. The hub keeps the row, so the data is not destroyed, but getting it back takes someone with an install key or hub DB access who also knows the id. That contradicts the hub README's 'any version can be restored'. Manual links have the same gap: manual-links.tsx:113 even shows 'Removed (it can be restored from the hub)', and nothing offers that restore. Rated medium: it happens in a less common flow, but one click wipes a community entry for every shop and there is no way back in the app. Letting TECH users remove entries fits the wiki design and is not a defect on its own.
also_reported_as: security: src/actions/xref.ts:71 Any user of any company, including a TECH or a self-signed-up shop, edits, merges and deletes the community cross-reference under the install's single hub key and the joining company's name

title: 'Add it to the cross-reference' publishes the part's private notes to every hub member, along with local '(own)' numbers and free-text 'fits' marked 'Fitted by a tech'
description: addPartToCrossRef sends notes: p.notes. That is the shop's internal Notes field on the part form, and nothing on the form says it may be shared. It goes to the community hub, where every member reads it in the entry and its history (and cannot delete revisions). Consigned items carry notes such as 'On consignment from <partner>'. The partNumber is sent unchanged, so the app's own local suffixes ('X (own)', 'X (<Partner name>)') become community part numbers. Each comma-separated fragment of the free-text 'Fits models' field is published as a fit with evidence 'tested' ('Fitted by a tech', the strongest evidence), under brand 'Generic' when the part has no brand. Elsewhere the app promises that only part numbers and counts are shared (most-used page footer).
failure_scenario: Create part 'QAPI7K3X-77 (own)' with Notes 'PRIVATE: we pay $1.10 from Joe Smith 555-0100; Mrs Jones owes us' and Fits 'most Janome, ask Bob'. On its page click 'Add it to the cross-reference'. Another hub member (a fresh install key) reading GET /v1/xparts/<id>/history receives notes 'PRIVATE: we pay $1.10 from Joe Smith 555-0100; Mrs Jones owes us', number 'QAPI7K3X-77 (own)', and fits [('ask Bob','tested'), ('most Janome','tested')].
suggested_fix: Don't send p.notes; send notes: null or let the user review the entry first by prefilling the XrefForm on /xref instead of posting directly. Strip a trailing ' (own)' or ' (<suffix>)' from partNumber, and send the base number the alt list holds. Send fits with evidence 'listed' or not at all, and require a real brand.
evidence:
e10.js: `numbers: Generic QAPI7K3X-77 (own)` / `notes box: PRIVATE: we pay $1.10 ...` / `fits: Generic, ask Bob\nGeneric, most Janome`.
As another member: `curl localhost:8080/v1/xparts/e2b40ec57787417bb46b71cb/history -H 'Authorization: Bearer <other key>'` -> `E2E Test Shop | PRIVATE: we pay $1.10 from Joe Smith 555-0100; Mrs Jones owes us | [{'brand': 'Generic', 'number': 'QAPI7K3X-77 (own)'}] | [('ask Bob', 'tested'), ('most Janome', 'tested')]`.
xref.ts:106-112: `notes: p.notes, numbers: [{ brand, number: p.partNumber }, ...], fits: splitList(p.fits).map((m) => ({ ..., evidence: "tested" }))`.
verifier_notes: confirmed: addPartToCrossRef (src/actions/xref.ts:98-121) posts to the hub straight from the part row. It sends notes: p.notes (the part form's plain 'Notes' box, part-fields.tsx:126-129, with no hint that it is shared), the partNumber exactly as stored including local suffixes, and every comma-separated 'Fits models' fragment with evidence 'tested', which the UI labels 'Fitted by a tech' (EVIDENCE_LABEL in lib/parts.ts). The brand becomes 'Generic' when the part has none. The button (parts/[id]/page.tsx:184) shows no preview or disclosure. title: Cross-reference edits overwrite the whole entry from a stale local copy (lost updates, including the supplier scan's where-to-buy links)
description: saveCrossRef rebuilds the entry from the install's local XPart copy (form text plus prev.fits/prev.sources) and PUTs it. PUT /v1/xparts/:id (stitchhub src/parts.mjs:240-258) replaces numbers, fits and sources with no version or updatedAt check. The local copy is refreshed only every 10 minutes (instrumentation.ts:12), or later when offline. Any hub-side change made after that sync is silently wiped by the next edit from the install. This includes other shops' edits, admin imports and the admin supplier scan (/v1/admin/xparts/sources/import).
failure_scenario: The admin runs the supplier scan, which attaches 'Sewing Parts Online, $12.99' to Janome HK-…. Within the next 10 minutes a tech whose install hasn't synced yet corrects the part name. The PUT carries the pre-scan sources ([]), and the scan's link is deleted.
suggested_fix: Send the base version, for example `baseUpdatedAt: prev.updatedAt` or the id of the last revision seen. The hub should answer 409 when the entry changed since then, and StitchBench should reload the entry and show the conflict. Alternatively, fetch the current entry from the hub right before building the PUT, and send only changed fields and sources.
evidence:
Private hub, t6.mjs:
  supplier scan: { attached: 1, updated: 0, unmatched: 0, unchanged: 0 }
  after the edit: 200 []
Hub PUT has no concurrency check: `UPDATE xparts SET name = $2 ... WHERE id = $1` then writeEntry() deletes and re-inserts all child rows.
verifier_notes: confirmed: Accurate. saveCrossRef (stitchbench src/actions/xref.ts:28-53) builds the PUT body from the form, whose text areas were filled from the install's local XPart copy, plus prev.fits and prev.sources. PUT /v1/xparts/:id (hub parts.mjs:240-258) takes a row lock but sends no base version and checks none, and writeEntry replaces every child row. The local copy is refreshed by the hub sync every 10 minutes (instrumentation.ts:12), and later still when offline or when the page has been open a while. Any hub-side change made after the last sync is silently undone by the next edit, including another shop's edit, an admin import or the supplier scan. The loss can be undone through the history UI, but nothing warns anyone that it happened.

title: Editing any cross-reference entry corrupts its 'where to buy' sources (comma prices/URLs, 3-decimal prices, currency, vendor names, notes)
description: The xref form round-trips sources through plain text: sourcesText writes 'vendor, url, 12.50' and parseSources splits each line on every comma. It takes the first part as the vendor, the first http(s) part as the URL and the first part that looks like a number as the price, and it forces currency 'USD' (line 114). Any comma inside a vendor name, URL or price is therefore misread. Prices with 3 decimals are silently dropped. Currency and the note field (kept only when vendor and url match exactly) are lost. Because the form re-submits every source on every save, fixing an unrelated field such as specs or name rewrites the community entry for all shops. Supplier-scan and API sources that carry a currency or note are affected most.
failure_scenario: (1) Where to buy = 'Big Supplier, https://big.example/foot, 1,000.50' gives $1.00. (2) 'Wawak, https://wawak.example/p?ids=12,34, 4.95' gives url '...?ids=12' and price $34.00. (3) 'Euro Parts, https://euro.example/f, 19.999' gives no price. (4) A hub source {vendor:'Canada Sew, Inc.', currency:'CAD', priceCents:1299, note:'ships from Toronto'}: a tech changes only Specs and saves, and the source becomes vendor 'Canada Sew', USD 12.99, no note, re-attributed to the editing shop.
suggested_fix: Stop round-tripping sources through comma text. Edit them as structured rows (vendor / url / price / currency / note inputs per source, with the source id in a hidden field). At minimum: parse the URL as the first 'https?://' token up to whitespace, parse the price with toCents on the last field only, keep `was.currency` and `was.note` when the id matches, and reject prices with more than 2 decimals instead of dropping them.
evidence:
Playwright against http://localhost:3100 (pw3.cjs, as a TECH), hub rows after save:
Wawak|https://wawak.example/p?ids=12|3400|USD
Big Supplier|https://big.example/foot|100|USD
Euro Parts|https://euro.example/f||USD
pw4.cjs: textarea before edit "Canada Sew, Inc., https://ca.example/p, 12.99"; after 'Save for everyone' with only specs changed: 8931cebc...|Canada Sew|https://ca.example/p|1299|USD||E2E Test Shop (was CAD, note 'ships from Toronto', byShop 'QA HCM Buyer').
Code: `const parts = line.split(",")...; const priceText = parts.find((p) => /^\$?\d+(\.\d{1,2})?$/.test(p)); ... currency: "USD"` (parts.ts:106-114).
verifier_notes: confirmed: parseSources (src/lib/parts.ts:105-117) splits each line on every comma. It takes parts[0] as the vendor, the first http(s) part as the URL and the first part that looks like a number as the price, and it always sets currency to 'USD', even when the previous source matched (the spread is overridden). Because xref-form.tsx:77 re-sends every source as text on each save, and saveCrossRef (xref.ts:41) replaces all sources on the hub, any edit to an entry rewrites them. On the hub, writeEntry (parts.mjs:183-187) gives any source whose id was lost (vendor contains a comma) a new id, attributes it to the editing shop, and drops its note. Non-USD sources, which the admin supplier-scan import and the API allow (parts.mjs:106, 497), are silently turned into USD. Some cases are user typos (1,000.50 and 19.999), but those are still stored wrongly or dropped without any error.
also_reported_as: code: src/lib/parts.ts:114 Editing a cross-reference entry in StitchBench relabels every where-to-buy price as USD and loses sources whose vendor contains a comma
code: src/lib/parts.ts:114 Editing a cross-reference entry rewrites every source's currency to USD

title: The same barcode in 12-, 13- or 14-digit form (UPC-A / EAN-13 / GTIN-14) doesn't match, and Excel's scientific-notation UPCs are imported silently
description: numberKey only upper-cases and strips punctuation, so '0045544319491' (EAN-13, the form the import page's own placeholder uses: '3148\t0442717314803'), '045544319491' (UPC-A, what most USB scanners send for a UPC-A symbol by default) and '00045544319491' (GTIN-14 from distributor files) are three different keys. scanCode (scan.ts:16) and the register's itemByCode (register.ts:49) both use that key, so an item imported from a line sheet in one form reads as 'isn't in your parts' when a scanner sends another form. The import also takes Excel's display form of a numeric UPC column ('7.44272E+11', which is what gets copied when a 12-digit number sits in a General-format cell) as a barcode, with no warning. Several different products then get the same lossy alt number (numberKey '744272E11').
failure_scenario: Import CL-3149 with UPC 0045544319491. Scanning 0045544319491 finds it. Scanning 045544319491 (12 digits), 45544319491 or 00045544319491 gives '... isn't in your parts.'. Separately, paste 'SKU\tUPC\tDescription...' rows whose UPC cells read 7.44272E+11. The preview shows the value without a warning, the rows import as 'added', and both items store altNumbers {7.44272E+11}.
suggested_fix: For all-digit codes of length 8, 12, 13 or 14 (and ideally with a valid check digit), normalise to one canonical key, e.g. GTIN-14 left-padded with zeros, and store it in numberKeys next to the raw key. Normalise scanned codes the same way in scanCode, itemByCode and addLine. In the import preview, flag barcodes matching /\d(\.\d+)?E\+\d+/i (and UPC cells that have lost leading zeros) and skip those rows.
evidence:
e9.js: `13 digits: {"ok":true,...CL-3149}` / `12 digits: {"ok":false,..."045544319491 isn't in your parts."}` / `11 digits: ... isn't in your parts.` / `14 digits: ... isn't in your parts.`
e11.js (d): `preview barcodes: [ '7.44272E+11', '7.44272E+11' ]` / `Imported: 2 added` / DB `XL-1|{7.44272E+11}|{XL1,744272E11}` and `XL-2|{7.44272E+11}|{XL2,744272E11}`.
verifier_notes: confirmed: numberKey (lib/parts.ts:27) only upper-cases and strips non-alphanumerics, so the 12-, 13- and 14-digit forms of the same GTIN are different keys. scanCode/findPart and itemByCode both match on that key. The import page's own placeholder shows a 13-digit EAN, while USB scanners send UPC-A as 12 digits by default, so an item imported in one form reads as 'isn't in your parts' when scanned in the other. Separately, Excel's General format shows numbers of 12 or more digits as '7.44272E+11', and that display text is what gets copied. The importer takes it as a barcode with no warning, and the preview shows it as a normal value. This matches the rubric's 'missing validation that stores bad data'. It can be recovered by editing the alt numbers, but scanning fails silently until then.

title: Marketplace ratings are trivially manipulated: seller unilaterally drives order to PAID and can defame buyers; sockpuppet 5-star inflation
description: The order state machine lets the seller alone advance an order to PAID (POST /orders/:id/paid, step('seller',['ACCEPTED']), market.mjs:449) without any buyer action or real payment — the 'buyer pays seller directly' model has no verification. The seller can then rate the buyer (RATE_FROM.seller=['PAID','SHIPPED','RECEIVED'], market.mjs:490-506), and the buyer can never rate back because RATE_FROM.buyer requires SHIPPED/RECEIVED, which the seller can withhold (and the seller can then cancel from PAID, OPEN includes PAID). So a seller can attach a permanent 1-star public rating to any buyer it transacts with, unanswerable. Separately, because listings may be priced at 0 (priceCents>=0, market.mjs:189-192) and registration only needs the community join key (shared among all members) rate-limited per-IP at 10/hour (server.mjs:124), a member can spin up a second install and mint unlimited 5-star seller ratings against itself with zero money moving, inflating its `sellerReputation` shown on every listing and via GET /v1/reputation/:installId.
failure_scenario: Defamation: buyer B places an order; seller S accepts, then S calls /paid (200) though B never paid, then S rates B 1 star ('Never paid, avoid') which is stored and shows in B's public asBuyer reputation; S cancels; B's attempt to rate S returns 409 ('you can rate the seller once the order has shipped'). Inflation: attacker registers a 2nd install, lists a $0 item, orders it from the 2nd install 5 times, accept+ship each, rate 5★ → asSeller {avg:5,count:5}.
suggested_fix: Gate buyer-rateable and seller-rateable states on mutual progress: only let the seller rate the buyer after the buyer has signalled payment (buyer-paid) or after SHIPPED, and let the buyer rate the seller whenever the seller could rate the buyer, so neither side can rate unanswerably. Consider ignoring ratings from orders where seller and buyer share contact/IP or where price is 0, and de-weighting reputation by distinct counterparties. At minimum, don't let a seller reach PAID + rate a buyer with no buyer participation.
evidence:
Reproduced:
  seller marks paid (buyer never paid): 200
  seller rates buyer 1: 200
  seller cancels: 200 CANCELLED
  buyer tries to rate back: 409 You can rate the seller once the order has shipped.
  buyer reputation: {"asBuyer":{"avg":1,"count":1},"recent":[{"stars":1,"comment":"Never paid, avoid","role":"buyer"...}]}
  listing at price 0 status 200 ; seller reputation after 5 self-made orders: {"avg":5,"count":5}
verifier_notes: confirmed: market.mjs order state machine: /orders/:id/paid is step('seller',['ACCEPTED']) (line 449) so the seller alone advances to PAID with no buyer action or payment. RATE_FROM.seller=['PAID','SHIPPED','RECEIVED'] but RATE_FROM.buyer=['SHIPPED','RECEIVED'] (line 490), and OPEN includes PAID (line 9) so the seller can cancel from PAID. Thus a seller can PAID+rate the buyer 1-star while the buyer can never rate back (409), producing an unanswerable public buyer rating shown via /reputation/:id and buyerReputation on every future order. Separately, listings allow priceCents>=0 (line 189-192) and /v1/register issues an install to anyone with the shared join key (server.mjs:124, per-IP 10/hr), so a member can self-register a second install, list a $0 item, and self-deal unlimited 5-star seller ratings. This is a concrete integrity/defamation problem, not merely a preference.
also_reported_as: qa: src/market.mjs:450 An order shipped before payment can never be marked paid: its invoice shows the full balance due forever
qa: src/market.mjs:490 Rating eligibility is controlled by the seller: non-shippers can't be rated, buyers can be 1-starred without paying, and repeat or sock-puppet orders inflate counts
code: src/market.mjs:490 A buyer can never rate a seller who took payment and didn't ship, or who cancelled after being paid
qa: src/market.mjs:470 A buyer can cancel an order after the seller has recorded payment, with no refund step

title: Multi-company install: every company's listings, sales, invoices, notes and star ratings are published under the one install's name
description: A hosted StitchBench with several companies has one hub install and one install name: the name of the company whose admin joined. The hub fills in the seller and buyer names from that install. Listings use `inst.name` as shop_name (market.mjs:229-230). Orders use `seller.name` / `me.name` as seller_shop / buyer_shop (market.mjs:334-335). Notes use `inst.name` (server.mjs:406-408). Ratings are keyed by install_id (order_ratings.rated_install_id). StitchBench never sends which company acted: createListing, placeOrder and pushPending send no seller/buyer company. The partner channel does handle this per company (shopRef/shopName in partners.mjs); the marketplace and notes do not. So company B's listing shows to every hub member as sold by company A. Company B's invoice (market/orders/[id]/invoice/page.tsx:30 prints `o.sellerShop`) carries company A's name in the header above company B's address and pay instructions. A company B note that showed its own name while pending (shared-posts.tsx uses p.shop.name) switches to company A's name after sync. The buyer's bad rating of a company B sale lowers company A's seller rating on every listing and on /market/shops/<installId>. That page also labels the other companies' listings 'Your listing', because ListingCard uses the raw `mine` flag. INSTALL.md documents this setup: one Railway copy holding several shops, and a repair shop hosting its sewing shops, which sell notions/fabric/thread, in the same install.
failure_scenario: The shared test install at :3100 joined the hub as 'E2E Test Shop'. I renamed my own company there to 'QA HubMkt Shop A' and listed 'QA orphan test ...' from it. On the hub that listing has shop_name = 'E2E Test Shop', and the order a buyer placed on it has seller_shop = 'E2E Test Shop'. Every other shop sees another company's name, and ratings from that sale go to that company.
suggested_fix: Give marketplace and notes a per-company identity the way partners.mjs does. StitchBench sends shopRef (the company id) and shopName with every listing, order, note and rating. The hub stores seller_shop_ref/seller_shop_name on listings, orders and posts, and keys reputation by (install_id, shop_ref). StitchBench fills in sellerShop/buyerShop from these fields and computes ListingCard's 'Your listing' from shopId, not the raw `mine` flag. Until then, block the marketplace for companies other than the one that joined on multi-company installs.
evidence: Reproduced (scratchpad orphan.js): psql stitchhub -> `select id, shop_name, install_id from listings where id='f3434c9d986249d0b1e61158'` => `f3434c9d...|E2E Test Shop|174f69093bc341658e210a14`; `select seller_shop, buyer_shop from orders where id='5b9cf7027eb243ebaf6213cb'` => `E2E Test Shop|QA Buyer ...`, while the listing was created by shop 'QA HubMkt Shop A'. Code: market.mjs:230 `const vals = [id, inst.id, inst.name, ...Object.values(f)];`, market.mjs:334-335 `seller.name, me.name`, server.mjs:408 `[id, inst.id, inst.name, ...]`.
verifier_notes:
confirmed: The hub keys identity only on the install. createListing sets shop_name = inst.name (market.mjs:229-230). Orders copy seller.name and me.name from the installs table (market.mjs:334-335). Posts use inst.name (server.mjs:406-408). StitchBench sends no per-company identity: createListing's listing JSON, placeOrder's body and pushPending's post JSON carry no shop ref or name. Multi-company plus hub is a supported setup: requireInstallAdmin's comment says one hub connection is shared by all companies, the listing page has a 'sameInstall' branch, and round 1 scoped listings and orders per company locally but never gave the hub a per-company identity. The invoice page prints o.sellerShop (the install name) as the header above company B's own sellerContact address and pay instructions. The shop page's ListingCard uses the raw `mine` flag. I recalibrated to medium: the problem only occurs on multi-company installs that joined as full members, and it causes wrong attribution and merged reputation, not access to another shop's data or wrong money totals.
confirmed: The code does what the finding says, and multi-company use of the marketplace is a supported flow. HubState is a single row (id=1), so one install key covers every company on a StitchBench. src/actions/hub.ts:22-23 says outright that the hub connection is shared by every company. The marketplace is meant to work per company: ownListing/ownOrder check shopId, and market/[id]/page.tsx:20-22 and :133 handle 'Listed by another company on this same StitchBench'. But createListing (src/actions/market.ts:29-70) sends no seller identity. placeOrder sends only buyerContact.name. pushPending sends only authorName. The hub then fills in names from the install: market.mjs:229-230 uses inst.name for listings.shop_name, market.mjs:334-335 uses seller.name/me.name for orders.seller_shop/buyer_shop, and server.mjs:406-408 uses inst.name for posts.shop_name. Ratings are keyed only by rated_install_id (market.mjs:47, 509-512). So company B's listings, orders and notes carry the joining company's name, the invoice header (invoice/page.tsx:30, o.sellerShop) shows company A's name, and B's ratings pool into A's reputation. I lowered the severity from high. No private data crosses tenants, and money is not misdirected: the invoice's address, phone and email and the pay instructions come from company B's own sellerContact and payInstructions, sent on accept (market.ts:210-214). It only happens on hosted installs with several companies that joined the hub as a member and use the marketplace, which is a less common flow. The effect is wrong attribution and reputation, not loss of data or money.
also_reported_as: code: src/market.mjs:230 On a hosted multi-company StitchBench, every company trades on the hub under one install's name and a shared rating

title: Hub: a blocked seller's listings stay ACTIVE in every member's feed and still accept new orders
description: Blocking an install (POST /v1/admin/installs/:id/block) only sets installs.blocked. POST /v1/orders loads the seller with 'SELECT id, name FROM installs WHERE id = $1' and doesn't check blocked. The blocked install's listings are not paused or removed, so they keep going out in /v1/changes as ACTIVE. Buyers keep ordering from a shop the admin has banned, and that shop can no longer see the orders (every call returns 403).
failure_scenario: The hub admin blocks a scam shop. Its 'cheap motor' listing stays on every shop's Browse page. Buyers keep sending orders, which sit in REQUESTED forever. Worse, orders the scam shop had already accepted still carry its payment instructions.
suggested_fix: In POST /orders, refuse with 409 when the seller is blocked. When an install is blocked, set its ACTIVE listings to PAUSED or REMOVED and bump seq so members pick up the change. Consider cancelling its open REQUESTED orders with a reason.
evidence: On my own hub: register 'Scam Shop X', list 'X cheap motor', block it (admin 200). Feed: 'blocked seller listing still in feed: ACTIVE'. R orders: 'order on blocked seller: 200 REQUESTED'. X: 'blocked seller can see it: 403 {"error":"The hub admin has blocked this install."}'.
verifier_notes: confirmed: Confirmed. The admin block route (server.mjs:537-541) only sets installs.blocked. POST /v1/orders (market.mjs:321) loads the seller without checking blocked, and nothing pauses or removes the blocked install's listings. They stay ACTIVE in /v1/changes, and new orders are accepted that the blocked seller can never see or act on. The shared hub already shows it: 'B's presser foot MUIMNZ0Y' from install 81647c51 (blocked=t by the market.spec cleanup) is ACTIVE on the hub and in the 3100 install's local Listing table. It affects a moderation flow, so medium.
also_reported_as: code: src/market.mjs:321 Blocking an install leaves its listings on the marketplace, and they still take orders

title: Catalog vandalism/data loss: part numbers on soft-deleted parts block reuse, and admin bulk import silently attaches to removed parts
description: checkNumbers (parts.mjs:137-151) and the bulk-import owner lookup (parts.mjs:373-378, used at :391) match part numbers via xpart_numbers WITHOUT excluding soft-deleted parts (`deleted=true`). (The sources-import query at :505 correctly adds `AND NOT p.deleted`, showing the omission is a bug, not a convention.) Consequences: (1) Any member can permanently 'squat' a (brand,number): create a part with that number, then DELETE it; the number stays owned by the removed part, so every other member's POST/PUT /xparts with that number gets 409 pointing at a part they cannot see or easily restore (the bench's local numberOwner won't find it because saveXPart deletes removed parts locally). (2) Admin POST /v1/admin/xparts/import counts a row as 'merged' and writes its new numbers/fits onto the soft-deleted part, so imported reference data is silently invisible to all members while the import reports success.
failure_scenario: Member B creates part with number XA123, then DELETEs it. Member A tries POST /xparts with XA123 → 409 'already on another part' pointing at the (invisible, removed) part; A cannot use that number. Admin then bulk-imports {numbers:[{Brother,XA123}], fits:[{Brother,CS6000i}]} → response {added:0, merged:1, skipped:0}, but the fit was added to the deleted part and never reaches any member via /v1/changes.
suggested_fix: In checkNumbers and the import owner lookup, join xparts and exclude soft-deleted parts (`AND NOT p.deleted`) as the sources-import already does — a live add should not collide with a removed part, and import should create a fresh part (or restore the removed one) rather than silently writing to deleted rows.
verifier_notes: confirmed: checkNumbers (parts.mjs:137-151) and the bulk-import owner lookup (parts.mjs:373-378) match xpart_numbers WITHOUT `AND NOT p.deleted`, whereas the sources-import query (parts.mjs:505) DOES exclude deleted parts -- an intra-file inconsistency proving it is an omission, not a convention. Consequence 1: a member can create a part with a number then soft-delete it; the number stays owned by the removed part, so any other member's live add of that number gets 409 pointing at a part they cannot see (bench saveXPart deletes removed parts locally, hub.ts:473). Consequence 2: admin POST /v1/admin/xparts/import counts the row as 'merged' and writes new numbers/fits onto the soft-deleted part, so the imported reference data is invisible to all members (never surfaces via /v1/changes because saveXParts drops deleted) while the import reports success. Mitigation note: the 409 returns the partId and /xparts/:id/restore is a member route, so the squat is recoverable via restore+merge, which caps severity.
also_reported_as: code: src/parts.mjs:137 A removed cross-reference part can't be restored from StitchBench, and its numbers stay locked so nobody can re-add them
code: src/parts.mjs:141 Hub: a removed cross-reference entry keeps its part numbers reserved forever, so they can never be added again from StitchBench

title: /v1/changes core sync feed can be wedged by oversized xpart entries (3000-fit cap, no feed byte cap)
description: cleanPart allows up to 3,000 fits per part, each with brand(60)+model(80)+source(300) (parts.mjs:77-92), so one part serializes to ~1.7 MB in /v1/changes (server.mjs:207-251, `xparts: await partsByIds(ids)` at :246) and in /xparts/:id/history. The changes feed limits by row count only (up to 2000 rows, app uses 1000) with no aggregate byte cap. A member (writeLimit 300 writes/hour) can create a few hundred such parts; when they fall in one change page the response exceeds V8's ~512 MB string limit and c.json throws RangeError (500), the same failure mode proven for the partner feed. Because every member's background sync (stitchbench src/lib/hub.ts:636 doSync) re-requests from the same cursor and only advances on success, a wedged page permanently stalls the community sync (manual links, notes, parts, listings) for ALL members from that seq forward.
failure_scenario: Member creates ~300 parts each with 3000 max-length fits over ~1 hour. Once ~300+ land in a single 1000-row /v1/changes page (~510 MB+), every member's sync GET /v1/changes hits RangeError → 500, and cursors stall; the whole community feed stops advancing.
suggested_fix: Lower the per-part fits cap to a sane maximum (e.g. 200-300) and/or cap the /v1/changes response by accumulated bytes, returning more:true with an advancing next cursor before the payload gets large, so no single feed page can exceed a safe size.
evidence:
Partial (per-part size measured, full-feed break not exhausted to avoid load on the shared box): one such part measured 1,741,093 bytes in /v1/changes and 1,741,167 bytes in history for a single revision:
  D. big part: 200 request bytes 1414900
  D. /v1/changes response bytes for 1 such part: 1741093 xparts: 1
  D. history bytes after 1 revision: 1741167
The partner-feed finding is the fully-reproduced instance of the identical root cause (no byte cap on a member-controlled concatenated feed).
verifier_notes:
confirmed: Same confirmed root cause as finding 0 on the core community feed. cleanPart allows up to 3000 fits/part, each brand(60)+model(80)+source(300) (parts.mjs:77-92), and /v1/xparts has NO body-limit middleware (only partner messages/invites got bodyLimit in round 28842a1), so a ~1.4MB xpart body is accepted. /v1/changes (server.mjs:207-251) serializes full parts via partsByIds and caps only by row count (limit up to 2000, app uses 1000) with no byte cap. On the app side doSync (bench src/lib/hub.ts:636-657) does `since = String(ch.next)` and updates the cursor only AFTER hubFetch succeeds, so a 500 aborts the loop with the cursor unadvanced and every member's subsequent sync re-fails on the same page -> the whole community feed (links, posts, figures, parts, listings) stalls at that seq, and new installs starting at cursor 0 can never page past it to onboard. Fixable only by an admin deleting the offending parts. Broader blast radius than finding 0.
confirmed: Same root cause as id 0, on the community feed. cleanPart (src/parts.mjs:77-92) allows up to 3000 fits, each brand<=60 + model<=80 + source<=300 (+brandKey/modelKey/evidence), plus max name/category/specs/notes. xparts.seq DEFAULT nextval('change_seq') (migrations/002:14) so a POST insert takes a seq. The /v1/changes feed (server.mjs:207-251) inlines full entries via `xparts: await partsByIds(ids)` (line 246) with no byte cap; `more` = rows.length === limit (row-count only). On the app side doSync's /v1/changes loop (src/lib/hub.ts:636-659) only writes `cursor` after a successful fetch and rethrows on 500, so a RangeError 500 permanently stalls the community sync for EVERY member. I independently measured one maximal part at 1,772,880 bytes in /v1/changes; 303 such parts cross V8 MAX_STRING_LENGTH, at which point c.json throws the same RangeError. Precondition higher than id 0: an authenticated member and sustained abuse (writeLimit 300 writes/hour, server.mjs:161), so ~303 giant parts within one 1000-row page needs just over an hour. Not fixed by 28842a1. Severity medium: DoS needing auth + sustained abuse, on non-critical shared reference data (manual links, notes, parts) that is recoverable by deleting the offending parts, though the blast radius (all members' sync) is broad.

title: Rolling back a merged part (the History button) silently drops every number, fit and source that came from the merged-away part
description: /merge moves the from-part's numbers and sources onto intoId (UPDATE … SET xpart_id), copies its fits and marks from deleted. If someone then uses 'Roll back to this' on the target to undo a wrong merge, revert runs writeEntry(). That deletes all of the target's numbers, fits and sources and re-inserts only the pre-merge snapshot. The merged-in data is not returned to the from-part, which stays deleted with nothing on it, so it disappears from the cross-reference. The only copy left is in the from-part's revisions, which StitchBench cannot reach (the part is deleted locally).
failure_scenario: A tech merges 'Bobbin case dup' (Babylock BL-…, fits BL137, plus where-to-buy links) into 'Bobbin case' by mistake, then clicks 'Roll back to this' on the 'added' revision of 'Bobbin case'. Afterwards no live part holds BL-…, the BL137 fit or those links, and the merged-away entry cannot be opened in the app.
suggested_fix: Make merge undoable as one step: record the from-id in the merge revision, and when reverting past a 'merged' revision, restore the from-part from its pre-merge snapshot (deleted=false, its numbers, fits and sources) in the same transaction. At minimum, refuse the revert (409) and explain how to unmerge.
evidence:
Private hub, t1.mjs:
  merged numbers: [ 'BL-424999', 'BC-424999' ]
  history actions: [ 'merged', 'added' ]
  after roll back of target: 200 [ 'BC-424999' ]
  parts holding BL-424999: []
verifier_notes: confirmed: Accurate. Merge (parts.mjs:261-301) moves the from-part's numbers and sources onto the into-part and copies its fits, then marks the from-part deleted. The from-part's 'merged' revision is saved after the move, so it is empty. The revert route (lines 325-346) runs the old snapshot through cleanPart and writeEntry, which deletes all of the target's numbers, fits and sources and puts back only the pre-merge set. Nothing restores the from-part. Its data survives only in its own older revisions, and StitchBench cannot reach those because the from-part is deleted locally and its detail page returns notFound. 'Roll back to this' is a normal UI action on the target's history, which shows 'Merged' and 'Added' entries. The dropped numbers become free rather than locked. The from-part can be brought back only by calling the hub API by hand.
also_reported_as: qa: src/parts.mjs:342 Rolling back a merged cross-reference entry drops the merged part's numbers, fits and sources (merge can't be undone)

title: Editing or rolling back a large cross-reference entry silently truncates it to 50 numbers / 3000 fits / 30 sources
description: cleanPart() caps numbers at 50 (line 66), fits at 3000 (line 77) and sources at 30 (line 94) with .slice(), with no error. Merge (UPDATE xpart_numbers SET xpart_id) and admin import (numbers and fits from many entries added to one part) have no such cap, so entries can legitimately grow past the limits, for example universal bobbins and needles that fit thousands of models. StitchBench's 'Fix this part' form then sends the whole entry back (numbersText/fitsText of every row). The PUT keeps only the first 50/3000/30, and writeEntry deletes the rest. Revert passes the snapshot through the same cleanPart, so a roll-back truncates too.
failure_scenario: 'Class 15 bobbin' has 80 numbers after a merge. A tech fixes a typo in the name. The hub stores only 50 numbers, 30 are gone without warning, and they are now free for other parts to claim.
suggested_fix: Reject over-limit input with a 400 instead of slicing, and use the same caps in merge and import (or raise the caps and enforce them everywhere). For PUT, compare with the stored entry and refuse to drop rows the client didn't show.
evidence:
Private hub, t1.mjs:
  merged count: 80
  after a name-only edit, numbers: 200 50
verifier_notes: confirmed: Accurate. cleanPart silently cuts lists with .slice: numbers to 50 (line 66), fits to 3000 (line 77) and sources to 30 (line 94). PUT and revert both run through cleanPart and then writeEntry, which deletes every child row before re-inserting the cut-down lists. Merge, admin import and the supplier-sources import have no such limits. The supplier scan is the most realistic trigger, since it attaches any number of sources to a part, keyed by URL. StitchBench's XrefForm fills the text areas with every number, fit and source, and parseNumbers, parseFits and parseSources have no limits either. So an ordinary name edit through the UI sends everything, and the hub silently drops the excess. Dropped numbers become free for other parts to claim.

title: Community 'most-used parts' list breaks for all members: sum(qty)::int overflows int32
description: GET /v1/usage/top aggregates community usage with `sum(qty)::int` and `sum(tickets)::int` (usage.mjs:82). Per-item qty is capped at 1,000,000 (line 22) and each stored row fits in int4, but the SUM across a member's rows and across months is not bounded and is cast back to int4. Any single member can POST /v1/usage with 2,000 items of qty=1,000,000 for two months (each POST is valid, 200), making sum(qty) = 4e9 which overflows int32. Every member's GET /v1/usage/top then returns 500 ('integer out of range'). The bad data persists, so the community 'Most used parts' page (stitchbench src/app/(app)/parts/most-used/page.tsx:62) is broken for everyone until an admin blocks the offending install (blocked installs are excluded by the query's `NOT i.blocked`, which is the only mitigation) or deletes the rows.
failure_scenario: Member sends `POST /v1/usage {month:'2026-09', items:[2000 x {number:'EVIL-1', qty:1000000}]}` and the same for 2026-08. Both return 200 ({ok:true,items:1}). Any member then opens the Most-Used page → GET /v1/usage/top → 500 for all callers.
suggested_fix: Aggregate in bigint and clamp before returning: `sum(qty)::bigint` (and tickets), returning the value as a string/number the client can render, or `LEAST(sum(qty), 2147483647)`. Optionally cap a member's total monthly qty. The per-request Map accumulation in usage.mjs:44-49 should also guard against overflow before insert.
verifier_notes: confirmed: usage.mjs:80-97 aggregates with `sum(qty)::int` and `sum(tickets)::int` (int4). Per-item qty is capped at 1,000,000 (line 22) and the Map dedups per number_key, but the SUM across a member's rows and across months is cast back to int4 with no clamp. A single member can POST two valid months of 2000x{number:'EVIL-1',qty:1000000} (each dedups to one row of 2e9, which fits int4), making the cross-month sum 4e9 which overflows int4. Every member's GET /v1/usage/top then errors 'integer out of range' -> 500 (app.onError). Bad data persists; the only mitigation is the query's `NOT i.blocked`, so it stays broken until an admin blocks the offending install. The community 'Most used parts' page (bench parts/most-used/page.tsx:62) does try/catch, so it degrades to an error rather than crashing, but the community total is unavailable to everyone.
also_reported_as: qa: src/usage.mjs:82 Most-used-parts top list can be broken for every member by one install (summed usage overflows int)
